name: commitlintrc

items.description: Level: 0 disables the rule. For 1 it will be considered a warning, for 2 an error
Applicable: always|never: never inverts the rule
Value: the value for this rule

extends.description: Resolvable ids to commitlint configurations to extend

parserPreset.description: Resolvable id to conventional-changelog parser preset to import and use

helpUrl.description: Custom URL to show upon failure

formatter.description: Resolvable id to package, from node_modules, which formats the output

plugins.description: Resolvable ids of commitlint plugins from node_modules

ignores.description: Additional commits to ignore, defined by ignore matchers

defaultIgnores.description: Whether commitlint uses the default ignore rules

description:
Hey team,

I've updated our commit‑lint setup to extend the conventional configuration (`@commitlint/config-conventional`). We're now using the *conventional‑changelog‑angular* parser preset, which lives in `./parser-preset.js`; the preset's `parserOpts` are left empty for now. If a commit fails validation, the help page at https://commitlint.js.org/#/guides-local-setup will be shown, and the output will be formatted with the `@commitlint/format` package.

The rules are fairly strict: the commit **type** must be one of `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`, or `chore` (error level, always enforced). The **subject** case is warned against if it is sentence‑case (warning level, never allowed). The **header** must not exceed 72 characters (error level, always enforced). We've also added two plugins—`commitlint-plugin-jira` and `commitlint-plugin-function`—to extend functionality. Commits matching the patterns `WIP*` or `merge commit*` are ignored, and the default ignore rules remain enabled.
